column1: # ported.tsv: what docs/history/carried.py holds the removals' deletions to, beyond the imports.
# Columns (tab-separated): side, kind, path (as the source repository names it), commits (comma-
# separated full SHAs of the source repository, or -), the commit of THIS repository that carries
#   port            upstream changed the path after the import's source (between the merge base of
#                   source and upstream, and the upstream measured); the commits are upstream's, the
#                   tip commit is the one that ported them and changes the path, and carried.py
#                   proves the tip holds every one of their changes
#   port-in-source  upstream changed the path, and the import's source already held the change: the
#                   fork had made it first. No commit here carried anything (-), and carried.py
#                   proves the source holds the change
#   port-void       nothing of upstream's change lands here (-), for one of two reasons, and
#                   carried.py measures which. Upstream changed lines this repository's
#                   adaptation removed: every conflict of the three-way merge is a region the
#                   tip removed, and the tip holds every other upstream change. Or upstream
#                   added lines about a value of the core SDK, which this repository does not
#                   declare: carried.py's CORE_SUBJECT names the value, holds that no Go file
#                   here names it and that a file the core keeps does, and pins the lines by
#                   their sha256. Either way the lines not carried are printed
#   port-delete     upstream deleted a path the import holds; the tip holds it no more. A path
#                   upstream MOVED is a port-delete row for the old path and a port row for the new
#                   one, which carried.py measures against the old path's merge base
#   fork-only       the import's source changed the path where upstream had not; the commits are the
#                   fork's, and the reason says why the change stands here
#   not-carried     the removal deletes a path no import projects
# carried.py picks the kind an upstream change needs from what it measures, and fails on a row
